question.text:
Find the truth set of $P(x) \Rightarrow Q(x)$ given the following predicates defined over the universal set $\mathbb{R}{:}$

  • $P(x):$ $x^2 \leq 9$

  • $Q(x):$ $5x - 3 \gt 7$
question.explanation:
Since $P(x) \Rightarrow Q(x) \equiv \neg P(x) \lor Q(x),$ the corresponding truth sets can be found as follows:

\begin{align*} T_{P \Rightarrow Q} &= T_{\neg P \lor Q} \\[5pt] &= T_{\neg P} \cup T_Q \\[5pt] &= \overline{T}_P \cup T_Q \end{align*}

Now, we note the following:

  • To find the the truth set of $P(x),$ we solve the inequality: \begin{align*} x^2 &\leq 9 \\[5pt] -3 &\leq x \leq 3 \end{align*} So, the truth set of $P(x)$ is $ T_P =[-3,3]. $ As a result, the complement is $ \overline{T}_P = (-\infty,-3)\cup(3,\infty). $
  • To find the the truth set of $Q(x),$ we solve the inequality: \begin{align*} 5x - 3 &\gt 7 \\[5pt] 5x &\gt 10 \\[5pt] x &\gt 2 \end{align*} So, the truth set of $Q(x)$ is $ T_Q = (2,\infty). $

Therefore, we have

\begin{align*} T_{P \Rightarrow Q} &= \overline{T}_P \cup T_Q \\[5pt] &= \big( (-\infty,-3)\cup(3,\infty) \big) \cup (2,\infty) \\[5pt] &= (-\infty,-3)\cup(2,\infty) . \end{align*}

example.title: Finding the Truth Set of an Implication

question.text:
$\qquad$ If $x$ is a multiple of $10,$ then $x$ is a multiple of $5.$

Which of the following is logically equivalent to the conditional predicate above?
question.choice1: $x$ is not a multiple of $10,$ or $x$ is a multiple of $5.$
question.choice2: $x$ is not a multiple of $10,$ and $x$ is a multiple of $5.$
question.choice3: $x$ is a multiple of $10,$ or $x$ is a multiple of $5.$
question.choice4: $x$ is a multiple of $10,$ and $x$ is a multiple of $5.$
question.choice5: $x$ is not a multiple of $10,$ or $x$ is not a multiple of $5.$
question.explanation:
Let's denote by $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ the following predicates:

  • $P(x){:}$ $x$ is a multiple of $10.$

  • $Q(x){:}$ $x$ is a multiple of $5.$

Then, our initial sentence can be written as $P(x) \Rightarrow Q(x),$ which is logically equivalent to

\[ \neg P(x) \lor Q(x). \]

The negation of $P(x)$ can be written as

  • $\neg P(x){:}$ $x$ is not is a multiple of $10.$

Therefore, the given sentence is logically equivalent to the following:

$\qquad$ $x$ is not a multiple of $10,$ or $x$ is a multiple of $5.$

example.title: Using Laws Involving Implications and Equivalences

question.text:
Consider the following predicates.

$\qquad$ $A(x):$ $x \in \mathbb {Z}.$ $\qquad$ $B(x):$ $-x\in\mathbb {Z}.$

Which of the following is equivalent to the biconditional predicate $A(x) \Leftrightarrow B(x)?$

  1. If $x \in \mathbb {Z}$ then $-x \in \mathbb {Z}$, and if $-x \in \mathbb {Z}$ then $x \in \mathbb {Z}.$
  2. $x \in \mathbb {Z}$ is equivalent to $-x \in \mathbb {Z}.$
  3. $x \in \mathbb {Z}$ if and only if $-x \in \mathbb {Z}.$
question.explanation:
A biconditional expression $P \Leftrightarrow Q \equiv (P \Rightarrow Q) \land (Q \Rightarrow P)$ can be read as shown below:

  • $P$ if and only if $Q$

  • $P$ is equivalent to $Q$

  • If $P$ then $Q,$ and if $Q$ then $P$

So, $A \Leftrightarrow B$ translates into the following sentences:

  • $x \in \mathbb {Z}$ if and only if $-x \in \mathbb {Z}.$

  • $x \in \mathbb {Z}$ is equivalent to $-x \in \mathbb {Z}.$

  • If $x \in \mathbb {Z}$ then $-x \in \mathbb {Z}$, and if $-x \in \mathbb {Z}$ then $x \in \mathbb {Z}.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I, II, and III."

example.title: Using Laws Involving Implications and Equivalences

question.text:
For the universal set $U,$ given by

\[ U = \big\{ 5,10,15,20,25,30,35 \big\}, \]

find the truth set of $P(x) \Leftrightarrow Q(x)$ for the following predicates:

  • $P(x):$ $x$ is odd.

  • $Q(x):$ $\sqrt{x}$ is integer.
question.explanation:
Since we have that

\[ P(x) \Leftrightarrow Q(x) \equiv \big(P(x) \land Q(x)\big) \lor \big(\neg P(x) \land \neg Q(x)\big), \] the corresponding truth set can be found as follows:

\begin{align*} T_{P \Leftrightarrow Q} = (T_P \cap T_Q) \cup (\overline{T}_P \cap \overline{T}_Q) \end{align*}

Notice that:

  • The truth set of $P(x)$ is \[ T_P = \big\{ 5,15,25,35 \big\} \] and its complement is \[ \overline{T}_P %= \overline{\big\{ 4,6,8,9,10 \big\}} = \big\{ 10,20,30 \big\}. \]

  • The truth set of $Q(x)$ is \[ T_Q = \big\{25 \big\} \] and its complement is \[ \overline{T}_Q %= \overline{\big\{ 2,5,10 \big\}} = \big\{5,10,15, 20, 30,35 \big\}. \]

Therefore, we have

\begin{align*} T_P \cap T_Q &= \big\{ 5,15,25,35 \big\} \cap \big\{ 25 \big\} \\[3pt] &= \big\{ 25 \big\} \\[10pt] \overline{T}_P \cap \overline{T}_Q &= \big\{ 10,20,30 \big\} \cap \big\{5,10,15, 20, 30,35 \big\} \\[3pt] &= \big\{ 10,20,30 \big\} \\[10pt] T_{P \Leftrightarrow Q} &= (T_P \cap T_Q) \cup (\overline{T}_P \cap \overline{T}_Q)\\[3pt] &= \big\{ 25 \big\} \cup \big\{ 10,20,30 \big\} \\[3pt] &= \big\{ 10,20,25,30 \big\}. \end{align*}
